title: Fallback variant interoperability maintenance and validation procedures
creator: Priya Raman
description: We need a repeatable maintenance and validation procedure for the fallback model variant compatibility matrix that covers tokenizer parity, context/sequence length behavior, KV cache interoperability, and tool/function calling parity. This ticket drives the operational runbook, automated sanity checks, and a lightweight regression suite that can be run as part of model onboarding and routing-policy changes. The goal is to reduce incidents where a routed fallback variant produces tokenization mismatches, KV cache corruption, or tooling failures when used as a transparent substitute in smart routing flows.
acceptance_criteria: A documented maintenance runbook exists with step-by-step checks for tokenizer, context length, KV cache, and function/tooling compatibility
Automated sanity tests (unit + integration) that detect tokenizer/context drift are added to the variant-compat pipeline and run in CI
A lightweight end-to-end regression job that simulates routing fallbacks across 3 representative workloads (chat, code, long-context summarization) completes within SLA and flags incompatibilities
Alerts and triage playbook created for failures with clear owner, rollback, and mitigation steps
At least two existing fallback variants audited and marked as 'verified' in the compatibility matrix using the new tooling
checklist: Draft maintenance runbook and approval by Runtime/Infra leads
Define canonical test corpus for tokenizer parity (multilingual + edge-case UTF + mixed whitespace)
Implement tokenizer parity unit tests (compare tokenization + detokenization for samples)
Add KV cache compatibility smoke tests (KV save/restore across variant switch)
Add function/tool calling contracts test (json schema enforcement + error mapping)
Integrate sanity checks into variant-compat CI pipeline
Create dashboard panel that tracks compatibility test pass rate per variant
Schedule quarterly sweep job and implementation in orchestration (cron with reporting)
updates: 2025-11-07: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Inference, and Developer Tools. Agreed scope focused on tokenizer, KV cache, context window behavior, and tooling/json contract checks. Action: Runtime to provide sample models and artifacts.

2025-11-20: Collected tokenizer edge-case corpus from logs and community fuzzing. Stored corpus in gs://redwood-test-artifacts/fallback-compat/tokenizer-corpus-v1. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tokenization+Corpus+Library

2025-12-03: Prototype tokenizer parity unit test added to runtime-infra/variant-compat repo. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-infra/pull/482. Notes: initial tests catch whitespace and Unicode normalization differences for two variant pairs.

2026-01-12: KV cache smoke test design reviewed. Approach: snapshot KV after prefix generation, switch to fallback variant, resume generation and verify continuity of attention cache semantics. Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KVCacheFallbackDesign

2026-02-02: Started building integration harness for routing fallback simulation. Harness simulates 1000 requests across chat/code/long-context flows and enacts variant switch on MLP failure. Initial run found a deserialization mismatch for variant v2b -> v1q on a subset of long-context tests. Issue filed ENG-64608.

2026-02-18: Review with QA and Developer Tools. Decided to add a compatibility flag in model registry for 'compat_kv_v1' until remediation completed. Temporary mitigation: runtime routes to non-fallback for high-risk customers (see rollout note in console-2026.02).

2026-03-03: Implemented alerting in Console for compatibility CI failures. New dashboard panel: Route Compatibility Health (runtime-1.22). Grafana link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/compatibility/route-health
2026-03-10: Finalizing runbook edits. Preparing canary with audited variants for a 2-week observation window. Next: QA to run regression job and mark at least two variants as verified.
